newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MARADONA VISITS MANAGER IN JAIL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARADONA VISITS MANAGER IN JAIL.

text.p: Soccer star Diego Maradona met for three hours Sunday with his manager Guillermo Coppola, who was jailed Friday on drug dealing charges.

The former Argentina captain had tried to visit Coppola for his 49th birthday Saturday at the jail in the town of Dolores, 180 miles (300 km) south of Buenos Aires, but was deterred by throngs of journalists and onlookers.
But police said Sunday Maradona was granted special permission to see Coppola outside of visiting hours and drove his Mitsubishi van into the precinct.

Coppola was detained Wednesday after Judge Hernan Bernasconi issued an international warrant for his arrest in connection with a police raid of his apartment, which turned up one pound (500 g) of cocaine.
Coppola says the drug was planted and said he was "totally innocent."
Since his arrest senior officials have tried to play down the friendship between him and President Carlos Menem and his Menem's private secretary Ramon Hernandez.
Maradona, banned from playing in Italy in 1990 and kicked out of the 1994 U.S. World Cup for drug use, has admitted his addiction and undergone rehabilitation treatments this year.
Bernasconi also ordered the arrest of Maradona's brother- in-law Gabriel Esposito and former Argentine national soccer player Alberto Tarantini, but Esposito was released late Thursday.
